title: Dividing with a Remainder
description: What the lemma says and why the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Divide 17 by 5: you get 3 groups of 5 and 2 left over. So 17 = 5 x 3 + 2. The leftover is always less than 5, otherwise you could make another group.

blocks.heading: The lemma
blocks.body: a = bq + r, where 0 <= r < b

blocks.heading: Remember
blocks.body:
q and r are unique
r can be 0
b must be positive

blocks.heading: Try it
blocks.body: Write 58 in the form 7q + r. 58 = 7 x 8 + 2, so q = 8, r = 2.

title: Euclid's Algorithm for HCF
description: Repeat the lemma until the remainder is zero to find the HCF fast.

blocks.heading: Why it works
blocks.body: Any common factor of a and b also divides r = a - bq. So HCF(a, b) = HCF(b, r), and the pair keeps getting smaller.

blocks.heading: Worked example
blocks.body: HCF(196, 38220): 38220 = 196 x 195 + 0. Remainder is already 0, so HCF = 196.

blocks.heading: Checklist
blocks.body:
Larger number first
Stop at remainder 0
Answer is the last divisor, not the last quotient

title: Prime Factorisation
description: Break numbers into primes using a factor tree and see why the result is unique.

blocks.heading: Building blocks
blocks.body: Primes are the atoms of numbers. 360 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5, and no other list of primes multiplies to 360.

blocks.heading: Method
blocks.body:
Divide by the smallest prime repeatedly
Move to the next prime when it stops dividing
Write the answer with exponents

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: Factorise 1001: 1001 = 7 x 11 x 13.

title: HCF and LCM from Primes
description: Use prime factorisations to get HCF and LCM and check with the product rule.

blocks.heading: Rules
blocks.body:
HCF: smallest power of each common prime
LCM: largest power of every prime present
HCF x LCM = a x b

blocks.heading: Why 3^n never ends in 0
blocks.body: A number ending in 0 needs both 2 and 5 as prime factors. 3^n has only 3s, so it never ends in 0.

blocks.heading: Traps
blocks.body:
HCF uses the smallest powers
The product rule is for two numbers only

title: Zeros of a Polynomial
description: What a zero means algebraically and on the graph.

blocks.heading: Definition
blocks.body: k is a zero of p(x) if p(k) = 0. For p(x) = x^2 - 4, both 2 and -2 are zeros because they make p(x) zero.

blocks.heading: On the graph
blocks.body: The curve of a quadratic is a parabola. Its zeros are where it cuts the x-axis. It can cut twice, touch once, or never meet the axis.

blocks.heading: Check
blocks.body: Is 3 a zero of x^2 - 2x - 3? p(3) = 9 - 6 - 3 = 0. Yes.

title: Sum and Product of Zeros
description: The relations between zeros and coefficients, and how to build a polynomial from its zeros.

blocks.heading: Relations
blocks.body: For ax^2 + bx + c: alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha x beta = c/a

blocks.heading: Verify
blocks.body: 3x^2 - 12x + 9: zeros 1 and 3. Sum 4 = 12/3, product 3 = 9/3.

blocks.heading: Build
blocks.body: Zeros 2 and -5: sum -3, product -10. Polynomial x^2 + 3x - 10.

blocks.heading: Watch out
blocks.body:
The minus sign in -b/a
a is the coefficient of x^2, not of x

title: Recognising a Quadratic
description: Rearrange any equation into ax^2 + bx + c = 0 and read the coefficients.

blocks.heading: Standard form
blocks.body: A quadratic equation has degree 2 once simplified. Expand brackets, move everything to one side, and combine like terms before deciding.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: (x - 2)(x + 1) = x^2 - 3 becomes x^2 - x - 2 = x^2 - 3, so -x + 1 = 0. The square terms cancel: not a quadratic.

blocks.heading: Rule
blocks.body:
a is never 0 in a quadratic
Read b and c only from the standard form

title: Forming Quadratics from Word Problems
description: Turn a story into an equation by choosing the unknown well.

blocks.heading: Method
blocks.body: Let the unknown be the quantity asked for. Translate each sentence into an expression. Set up the equality the problem describes. Rearrange to standard form.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 306. Let the smaller be x: x(x + 1) = 306, so x^2 + x - 306 = 0.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: A train covers 480 km at speed x km/h. If it were 8 km/h slower it would take 3 h more: 480/(x - 8) - 480/x = 3, which simplifies to x^2 - 8x - 1280 = 0.

title: Splitting the Middle Term
description: The core factorisation technique, step by step.

blocks.heading: The technique
blocks.body: For ax^2 + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is a x c and whose sum is b. Rewrite bx as the sum of those two terms, then factor by grouping.

blocks.heading: Example with a = 1
blocks.body: x^2 + 5x + 6: product 6, sum 5 gives 2 and 3. (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0, so x = -2 or -3.

blocks.heading: Signs
blocks.body:
Product positive, sum positive: both positive
Product positive, sum negative: both negative
Product negative: one of each, larger magnitude takes the sign of b

title: The Quadratic Formula
description: Solve any quadratic with the formula and know when to reach for it.

blocks.heading: Formula
blocks.body: x = [-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / 2a

blocks.heading: When to use it
blocks.body: Use the formula when the middle term will not split neatly, or when the roots are irrational. It always works when b^2 - 4ac >= 0.

blocks.heading: Common slips
blocks.body:
Write -b, then square b separately
Divide the whole numerator by 2a
Simplify the square root before dividing

title: Word Problems and Checking Roots
description: Set up, solve, then reject roots that make no sense.

blocks.heading: Reject impossible roots
blocks.body: Lengths, ages, counts and speeds cannot be negative or fractional when the story says they are whole. Always check both roots against the situation.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: A rectangle has area 60 and its length is 7 more than its breadth. b(b + 7) = 60 gives b^2 + 7b - 60 = 0, (b + 12)(b - 5) = 0. b = -12 is rejected; breadth 5, length 12.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: Two numbers differ by 3 and their product is 54: x(x + 3) = 54, x^2 + 3x - 54 = 0, (x + 9)(x - 6) = 0, so 6 and 9, or -9 and -6 if negatives are allowed.

blocks.heading: Always
blocks.body:
Substitute each root back into the original equation
Answer the question asked, not just x

title: The Discriminant
description: Predict the type of roots without solving.

blocks.heading: Discriminant
blocks.body: D = b^2 - 4ac

blocks.heading: Three cases
blocks.body:
D > 0: two distinct real roots
D = 0: two equal real roots
D < 0: no real roots

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: x^2 + x + 1 = 0: D = 1 - 4 = -3, no real roots.

title: Finding Unknown Coefficients
description: Use D = 0 to find a parameter that gives equal roots.

blocks.heading: Method
blocks.body: Write D in terms of the unknown, set it equal to 0, solve the resulting equation. Check that a is still non-zero.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: 2x^2 + kx + 3 = 0 has equal roots: k^2 - 24 = 0, so k = +/- 2 sqrt 6.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: kx(x - 2) + 6 = 0 has equal roots: kx^2 - 2kx + 6 = 0, D = 4k^2 - 24k = 0, so k = 6 (k = 0 rejected).

title: Velocity and Time
description: The first equation of motion and the meaning of acceleration.

blocks.heading: Acceleration
blocks.body: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second. If a car goes from 10 m/s to 20 m/s in 5 s, its velocity changed by 10 m/s over 5 s, so a = 2 m/s^2.

blocks.heading: First equation
blocks.body: v = u + at

blocks.heading: Units
blocks.body:
Velocity in m/s
Acceleration in m/s^2
Time in s
Convert km/h by multiplying by 5/18

title: Displacement Equations
description: The second and third equations and how to choose between them.

blocks.heading: Choosing
blocks.body: List what you know and what you want. If time is not involved, use v^2 = u^2 + 2as. If final velocity is not involved, use s = ut + (1/2)at^2.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: A ball dropped from rest falls for 3 s (a = 10 m/s^2): s = 0 + 0.5 x 10 x 9 = 45 m.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: A bike at 15 m/s brakes at -3 m/s^2 to rest: 0 = 225 + 2(-3)s, so s = 37.5 m.

blocks.heading: Signs
blocks.body:
Choose the direction of motion as positive
Retardation gives negative a

title: Writing and Balancing Equations
description: From word equation to balanced symbol equation with states.

blocks.heading: Why balance
blocks.body: Atoms rearrange in a reaction but none appear or vanish. A balanced equation shows this with equal atom counts on both sides.

blocks.heading: Steps
blocks.body:
Write correct formulas
Count atoms of each element
Adjust coefficients, starting with the element in the fewest formulas
Balance H and O last
Recheck everything

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: Zn + HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2. Cl: 1 vs 2, so 2HCl. Now H: 2 vs 2. Balanced: Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2.

blocks.heading: Example
blocks.body: C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. C: 3CO2. H: 4H2O. O on right: 6 + 4 = 10, so 5O2. Balanced: C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O.

title: Types of Reactions
description: Combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement and redox with everyday examples.

blocks.heading: Combination and decomposition
blocks.body: Combination: two substances form one (CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2). Decomposition: one breaks into several, often by heat, light or electricity (2H2O -> 2H2 + O2 by electrolysis).

blocks.heading: Displacement
blocks.body: A more reactive element pushes out a less reactive one: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu. The blue solution turns green.

blocks.heading: Double displacement and redox
blocks.body: Ions swap partners: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl (white precipitate). In redox one substance gains oxygen (oxidised) while another loses it (reduced).

blocks.heading: Spotting them
blocks.body:
Two in, one out: combination
One in, many out: decomposition
Element swaps with element: displacement
Ions swap: double displacement
